newsitem.title: USA: WCE trading unaffected by Red River flooding.
newsitem.headline: WCE trading unaffected by Red River flooding.

text.p: At the Winnipeg Commodity Exchange, where prices are set for many of Canada's key crops, traders were busy buying and selling grain despite the surging Red River 2-1/2 blocks away nearing a record high crest.
"With respect to the Winnipeg Commodity Exchange, it's business as usual," said Don Thompson, assistant trading floor manager for the exchange.

Thompson said the building housing the exchange is 20 feet higher than the river and should survive even the worst flooding. Telephone and electrical systems are on upper floors and out of danger should flood waters threaten, he said.
"Even the worst case scenario does not impact us," he said.

About 8,800 Winnipeggers fled their homes this week as the rising river seeped through dikes shielding five city streets and inundated Canadian farmland covering an area twice the size of Hong Kong. Those dikes were repaired.
Manitoba's capital is protected by a 25-mile (40-km) dike southwest of the city that was completed on Wednesday.
But authorities were worried the hastily built dike may break under the pressure of the river, which already has flooded 800 square miles (2,100 sq km) of Manitoba land.
